key_idea: Rotation and motion each form one interval, so the only useful plan is: rotate in place by phi, then drive while still turning (circle of radius v/w), then drive straight along the tangent to the target; minimise over phi.
sketch: Mirror y to fix the turn direction (try both). For a given phi rotate the target by -phi; if it lies outside or on the turning circle centred (0,R), the arc angle and tangent length follow from atan2/acos, time = (phi+theta)/w + b/v. The feasible phi set is bounded by angles where the target lies exactly on the circle (ending on the arc), which can be the optimum, so those two angles alpha-asin(d/2R) and alpha-pi+asin(d/2R) are evaluated explicitly. Elsewhere a 400k-point grid on phi plus a local ternary refinement is used. Pitfalls: the same rotation direction applies to the in-place and arc phases, targets inside the circle are infeasible for that phi, and theta needs careful mod 2pi. Checked numerically that an initial straight segment never helps.
